title: AnalysisResult
description: Aggregated intelligence report for a repository.

analyzer.description:
Name and version of the tool that wrote the report. Empty in
reports from before versioning.

architecture_details.description:
Layers found in the code, the imports between them, a confidence
level and the evidence behind it.

blank_lines.description: Blank lines across all recognised source files.

circular_imports.description:
Groups of files that import each other, each as its shortest cycle
(the last file imports the first), shortest first.

comment_lines.description: Comment-only lines across all recognised source files.

coverage.description:
How much of the code the dependency analysis covered: files whose
imports were followed, imports that did not resolve and languages
that were not analyzed. Dead code and cycles only speak for the
covered part.

cycle_details.description:
The same cycles, in the same order, each with whether it closes
through runtime imports only, needs a possible edge, or needs a
type-only import.

dead_code.description: Files unreachable from any entry point via dependency graph traversal.

dead_code_details.description:
The same files with a confidence level and the reason for it, most
certain first.

dependencies.description:
Typed dependency facts: every import, re-export, worker, process,
configured entry and possible dynamic load found, with its kind,
resolution, certainty and evidence. Unresolved and external imports
are kept too. Sorted by source file and position.

dependency_graph.description:
Directed import graph: `file → [files it imports]`. A projection of
`dependencies`: the targets of its resolved facts, per source file.

file_breakdown.description: Per-file breakdown, sorted by LOC descending.

schema_version.description:
Version of the report's shape; see [`SCHEMA_VERSION`]. Reports from
before versioning read as 0.

total_loc.description:
Total code lines across all recognised source files.  Comment-only
and blank lines are excluded; see `comment_lines` and `blank_lines`.

usage.description:
How each file is used: confirmed from the program's entry points,
possibly, for types only, by tests only or by tooling only, with the
path from the entry that reaches it; unreachable files are the
dead-code candidates.

workspaces.description: Workspaces (monorepo packages) declared at the root, if any.

Analyzer.description: The tool that produced a report.

ArchitectureInsight.description: Layers, the imports between them, and how confident the result is.

evidence.description: Short, human-readable reasons for the result.

flows.description: Import counts between layers, largest first.

layers.description: Layers in top-down order (UI, Routes, Middleware, Services, Data).

Certainty.description: How sure the analysis is that the dependency exists.

oneOf.description: An import statement or call written in the source.
A declaration that loads a file: Rust `mod name;`.
Inferred from a call, a string or a framework convention.
May happen; the target is not known statically.

CodeSign.description: What a file's code shows about its layer, and where.

line.description:
1-based line of the match; 0 when the whole file is the sign
(`.vue`, `.svelte`).

sign.description: What matched: a route (`GET /users`) or the text found (`@Entity(`).

Confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports a conclusion.

Coverage.description: How much of the repository the dependency analysis covered.

analyzed_files.description: Source files whose imports were followed.

imports.description: What happened to the imports in the analyzed files.

not_analyzed.description:
Languages whose imports CodeDna does not follow, with file counts,
most files first. Dead code and cycles say nothing about these files.

parse.description:
How the files read with a syntax parser (JavaScript, TypeScript and
component scripts) parsed.

source_files.description: Files in a language that imports other files.

summary.description:
One sentence for people, e.g. "Imports followed in 120 of 140 source
files (85%); 3 of 410 internal imports unresolved; not analyzed:
Go (20 files)".

unreadable_files.description: Source files in a followed language that could not be read.

unresolved.description:
Imports of the repository's own code that matched no file, first
few by path and line.

Cycle.description: One group of files that import each other.

files.description: The files in import order; the last imports the first.

CycleKind.description: What it takes to close a cycle.

oneOf.description: Runtime imports only: the files load each other when they run.
Needs an import that may load one of several files.

Needs a type-only import, erased at runtime: harmless when the code
runs, though it still ties the files together.

DeadCodeCandidate.description: A dead-code candidate with how sure CodeDna is and why.

conditions.description: What may still load it, for a possible or unknown candidate.

evidence.description:
Lines that back the reason: where the name is mentioned, or the
dynamic loader that may load the file.

status.description:
Whether it is unreachable within what was analyzed, possibly loaded,
or unknown because an unresolved import may name it.

DeadStatus.description:
Whether an unreachable file is truly unreachable within what CodeDna
could analyze.

oneOf.description: Nothing the analysis saw could load it.

Something reached may load it: a shadowed `require`, a text-scan
fallback, a computed import whose fixed part points at it, or a file
that is itself possibly loaded.

An import from a reached file could not be resolved and might name
it, so coverage is incomplete.

condition.description:
When the dependency applies, if not always: `dynamic` for
`import()`.

source.description: The file that depends on something.

specifier.description:
The dependency as written: an import path, a module name, a file
name, or the target's own path for convention facts.

targets.description:
Files the specifier resolved to; empty unless `resolution` is
`resolved`. A Python import can load several (its packages'
`__init__.py` files and the module).

DependencyFacts.description: Every dependency fact in a report.

adapters.description: The framework adapters active in each package.

entries.description:
Files a framework, a package manifest or a test runner loads without
an import: one `configured_entry` fact per file, whose source and
evidence are the manifest declaring it. Kept apart from `facts`, which
`dependency_graph` projects, because a manifest is not a graph node.
Sorted like `facts`.

facts.description: Sorted by source, line, span, specifier and kind.

rules_version.description: See [`RULES_VERSION`]. 0 in reports from before facts.

DependencyKind.description: What kind of dependency a fact records.

oneOf.description:
Code loaded when the source runs: `import`, `require`, `import()`,
Python `import`, Rust `mod`.
Types only, erased at runtime: `import type`, `export type ... from`.
Exports of another module passed on: `export ... from`.
A file started in a worker thread: `new Worker("./w.js")`.
A file started in another process: `spawn("tsx", ["job.ts"])`.
A file referenced by URL: `new URL("./w.ts", import.meta.url)`.

A module a framework loads from configuration or by convention:
Django settings strings, installed apps and app modules.

Something that may be loaded, but whose target is only known at
runtime: ``import(`./pages/${name}`)``.

file.description: The file the fact was read from.

line.description:
Line number, from 1. Absent for facts from a convention rather than
a line, such as Django app modules.

rule.description:
Id of the rule that produced the fact, e.g. `js.import`,
`python.from_import`, `rust.mod`.

span.description:
Byte range `[start, end)` of the specifier in the file, when cheap
to know.

FileInfo.description: Per-file metadata produced by the analysis pipeline.

file.description: Path to the file (relative to the scanned root where possible).

loc.description: Code lines in the file: comments and blank lines are not counted.

FileUsage.description:
A file that is reached, but not confirmed: how, and the path from the
entry point that reaches it.

path.description:
The entry point first, then each file it leads through, ending with
this file.

FrameworkAdapter.description: A framework adapter active in one package, and why.

line.description: The manifest line declaring the dependency, when there is one.

manifest.description: The package manifest that activates it.

version.description:
Version of the adapter's rules; its facts carry rule ids ending in
`@v<version>`.

ImportCounts.description:
Import counts across the analyzed files. Each distinct import in a file
counts once.

ambiguous.description:
Resolved imports that could load one of several files (a subset of
`resolved`).

external.description: Imports of packages outside the repository.

inferred.description:
Resolved imports whose target CodeDna inferred rather than read from
configuration, e.g. a built `dist/x.js` mapped to `src/x.ts` (a
subset of `resolved`).

internal.description: Imports of the repository's own files: `resolved + unresolved`.

ImportEdge.description: One import from a file in one layer to a file in another.

LanguageGap.description: A language CodeDna does not follow imports for.

Layer.description: One architectural layer found in the code.

confirmed_by_code.description: Files whose code shows the layer (route handlers, models, …).

dirs.description: Up to three folders that hold most of its files.

examples.description: A few of its files and why each is here, code-backed ones first.

files.description: Number of source files assigned to it.

placed_by_imports.description: Files placed only by what imports them and what they import.

LayerFlow.description: Import edges from one layer to another.

examples.description: A few of the imports, by path.

Location.description: A line in the repository that backs a finding.

file.description: Path relative to the repository root.

ParseCounts.description: Files read with a syntax parser, by how far they got.

failed.description:
Not parsed at all; only possibilities from a text scan are
reported for these files, and they add no edges.

failures.description:
The first syntax error of the first few partial or failed files, by
path.

partial.description:
Parsed with syntax errors the parser recovered from; their facts
come from the recovered tree.

ParseFailure.description: The first syntax error in a file that did not fully parse.

file.description: Path relative to the repository root.

Placement.description: Why one file is in its layer.

code.description: The code that shows the layer, when it agrees.

file.description: Path relative to the repository root.

matched.description:
What placed it: the folder or file name, the settings prefix, the
code sign, or the files it sits between.

name_said.description:
The folder or file name the code overruled and the layer it
suggested (`services/ (Services)`), when they disagreed.

oneOf.description: Found among the scanned files; `targets` lists them.

A package from outside the repository (npm, PyPI, the standard
library, ...).
Points into the repository but matched no file.

Could be one of several files; `targets` lists every candidate (two
workspace packages with the same name, say).
The specifier cannot be resolved statically, e.g. a template literal.

UnresolvedImport.description: One import of the repository's own code that matched no file.

file.description: Path relative to the repository root.

import.description: The import as written, e.g. `./missing` or `@app/core`.

UsageKind.description: How a file is used, by the strongest evidence that reaches it.

oneOf.description: Reached from the program's entry points through runtime imports.

Reached from the program only through an import that may load one of
several files (an ambiguous import or a lazy pattern).

Reached from the program only through type-only imports, or from a
declaration file: used by the type checker, not at runtime.
Reached only from tests.

Reached only from build or development tooling: configs, stories,
task runners.
Not reached from any entry point: a dead-code candidate.

UsageReport.description:
How every analyzed file is used. Confirmed files are only counted;
unreachable files are the dead-code candidates.

files.description: Files reached, but not confirmed, sorted by path.

UsageSummary.description: How many files are used in each way.

Workspace.description: One workspace declaration and the packages it resolves to.

manifest.description: The file that declares it, relative to the root.

tool.description: The tool that owns the workspace, e.g. "pnpm" or "Cargo".

databases.description: Databases found in its own manifests.

depends_on.description:
Other packages of the repository it uses, by manifest dependency or
by import.

files.description: Source files in the package (a nested package's files are its own).

frameworks.description: Frameworks found in its own manifests.

name.description: The name from its manifest, or the directory name.

path.description: Its directory, relative to the root (e.g. `./packages/ui`).
